newsitem.title: UK: BT joins forces with C5 for N.Ireland retuning.
newsitem.headline: BT joins forces with C5 for N.Ireland retuning.

text.p: Channel 5 and British Telecom have formed a partnership to retune homes in Northern Ireland before the launch of the terrestrial television station, the two said in a statement.

BT will act as Channel 5's agents to retune video and other equipment affected by the new channel's signal, a task that will create employment lasting some six months for around 150 people. BT will recruit the temporary staff and supervise their work.

Some 350,000 households in Northern Ireland will be invited to test their video and satellite equipment when a trial Channel 5 transmission is carried out in January. Those experiencing interference will arrange for a retuning visit.
Channel 5, due to begin broadcasting on March 30, has hired an army of several thousand retuners in the rest of the United Kingdom who are visiting households to check video equipment.
The Northern Ireland method, in which only those reporting interferece in test transmissions are visited, could be adopted in other areas to speed up the retuning operation.

Channel 5 is owned by a consortium of British companies United News & Media Plc and Pearson Plc plus Luxembourg broadcaster CLT and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
